review_status: research-derived synthetic seed; generated sequences require human review before release claims
methodology: The cases are role-varied, source-grounded stimuli rather than copied employer questions. Expected moves encode public first-party interview behavior: clarify and communicate, establish a core solution, apply it, examine trade-offs and failures, and validate the result. Deterministic gates test atomicity, citations, source independence, repetition, breadth, progression, and work-sample cadence; an optional independent model judge scores the semantic experience.

topics.label: Bias and variance
topics.evidence: High bias can underfit systematic structure, while high variance makes a model sensitive to the sampled training data. Model capacity, regularization, and data volume influence this balance.

topics.label: Validation and data leakage
topics.evidence: Validation data should represent unseen use and remain isolated from training decisions. Time-dependent problems often require chronological splits so future information cannot leak into earlier predictions.

topics.label: Metrics for imbalanced classification
topics.evidence: Accuracy can hide poor minority-class performance. Precision and recall expose different error costs, and decision thresholds should reflect the operational cost of false positives and false negatives.

topics.label: Production drift and retraining
topics.evidence: Production inputs and outcomes can change after deployment. Monitoring feature distributions, prediction quality, and delayed labels helps distinguish drift from service incidents and guides retraining decisions.

topics.label: Retrieval and grounding
topics.evidence: A retrieval-augmented system selects evidence before generation so answers can be grounded in inspectable context. Retrieval quality and answer faithfulness are separate failure surfaces.

topics.label: End-to-end AI evaluation
topics.evidence: Evaluation should include representative answerable and unanswerable requests. Retrieval recall, citation correctness, unsupported claims, latency, and cost measure different aspects of an AI application's behavior.

topics.label: Diagnosing retrieval failures
topics.evidence: A missing answer can result from parsing, indexing, query formulation, retrieval ranking, or generation. Inspecting intermediate evidence and traces helps localize the failing stage before changing models.

topics.label: Quality latency and cost
topics.evidence: Larger context and more model calls may improve some answers but increase latency and cost. A production design should choose budgets against measured quality gains and user-facing response requirements.

topics.label: Time and space complexity
topics.evidence: Asymptotic analysis describes how runtime and memory grow with input size. Two solutions with the same broad complexity can still differ in constants, allocation behavior, and suitability for expected inputs.

topics.label: Hash table behavior
topics.evidence: Hash tables use a hash function to map keys into storage locations. Collisions must be resolved, and excessive collisions or resizing can change expected constant-time behavior.

topics.label: Small interface design
topics.evidence: A useful interface makes inputs, outputs, error behavior, and ownership clear while hiding implementation details. Small contracts are easier to test and change than interfaces that expose internal state.

topics.label: Tests and edge cases
topics.evidence: Tests should cover ordinary behavior, boundaries, invalid inputs, and prior regressions. When a test fails, reducing the case and tracing state changes can separate a faulty assumption from an implementation defect.

topics.label: Product goals and constraints
topics.evidence: A ranking system needs a defined user action, candidate population, traffic scale, freshness target, and latency budget. The product objective and harmful side effects determine what the system should optimize.

topics.label: Candidate generation and ranking
topics.evidence: A common architecture retrieves a manageable candidate set and applies a more expensive ranker afterward. Features needed online must be available consistently between training and serving.

topics.label: Labels and feedback loops
topics.evidence: Interaction logs provide abundant but biased labels because the deployed policy controls what users see. Exploration can improve learning but may reduce short-term user experience.

topics.label: Serving failures and fallbacks
topics.evidence: Online feature outages, stale data, or model-server timeouts should not take down the product. Bounded timeouts, observable fallbacks, and a simpler safe ranker limit the impact of failures.

topics.label: Offline and online evaluation
topics.evidence: Offline ranking metrics speed iteration but do not fully predict user impact. Guardrailed online experiments measure product outcomes while monitoring latency, reliability, and harmful distribution shifts.

topics.label: Delivery semantics and scale
topics.evidence: A notification design must establish channels, traffic, latency, ordering, duplication tolerance, user preferences, and durability. Different products may choose at-most-once or at-least-once delivery.

topics.label: Queue and worker architecture
topics.evidence: A durable queue separates request handling from channel-specific workers. Partitioning, retry scheduling, provider adapters, and preference checks form explicit component boundaries.

topics.label: State and idempotency
topics.evidence: Idempotency keys and delivery state reduce duplicate effects during retries. Retention, query patterns, write volume, and consistency requirements influence the storage choice.

topics.label: Backpressure and provider outages
topics.evidence: A slow downstream provider can grow queues and exhaust workers. Rate limits, circuit breakers, bounded retries, dead-letter handling, and per-channel isolation contain the failure.

topics.label: Operational validation
topics.evidence: Delivery latency, success rate, retry volume, queue age, and dead-letter counts reveal different operational failures. Load tests and failure injection validate behavior before incidents occur.
